obligations.note: Corpus is 212/214: sym/071 and sym/076 remain, unapproved (REQ-006).

obligations.text: Lovelace.Run.Tests integration tests reproduced or matched
desktop platform decision: Windows-only vs Windows/Linux/macOS
zero-dependency strategy as an explicit engineering decision

rows.title: Preserve scalar, vector, matrix, and higher-rank array distinctions.
Preserve shape, rank, strides, and element ordering.
Match indexing, negative/invalid indices, partial indexing, and slicing.
Implement reshape, transpose, squeeze, expand, flatten, concat, and append.
Match broadcasting rules and their error messages.
Match reductions, including axis behavior.
Preserve typed-field arithmetic without silently falling back to machine floating point.
Match dot products, matrix multiplication, determinants, inverses, trace, rank, and linear-system solving.
Test zero-dimensional, empty, singular, non-square, and incompatible-shape cases.
Verify matrix identities on generated exact inputs.
Implement the interactive Lovelace REPL.
Preserve multiline statement accumulation.
Support editing, history, and keyboard navigation.
Preserve interactive commands and help.
Maintain engine state between commands.
Match precision handling and _ result behavior.
Match errors, cancellation, and output formatting.
Match arithmetic and rendering across real and imaginary components.
rows.note: DFT arms and rendering now match the oracle at 25+ digits, including zero-imaginary Complex elements; broader complex arithmetic is not yet differentially clean.

rows.title: Preserve arbitrary precision.
rows.note: Arbitrary precision is preserved through the decimal complex transform; the fixed-width optimized representations (CPLX-003) are absent.

rows.title: Support the C# fixed-width optimized representations where their observable performance contract matters.
Promote to arbitrary precision without silently saturating or losing exactness.
Verify optimized results against arbitrary-precision results.
Preserve real-to-complex coercion and domain behavior.
Deliver an actual native desktop shell on the agreed supported platforms.
Preserve editor, workspace, graph, and logs panes.
Preserve the symbolic inspector.
Support multiple independent documents and engines.
Preserve per-document precision and execution state.
Execute scripts asynchronously without blocking input or rendering.
Support cancellation with consistent committed-state behavior.
Preserve incremental execution and visible statement status.
Restore window layout, documents, recent files, and settings.
Implement crash recovery for unsaved buffers.
Syntax highlighting.
Context-aware autocomplete using the live builtin registry.
Bracket matching and automatic indentation.
Find/replace, go-to-line, and editing shortcuts.
Inline diagnostics with accurate source positions.
Correct IME, clipboard, and Unicode handling.
Per-tab undo/redo and selection preservation.
Efficient editing of large scripts.
Browse variables with their kinds and structured projections.
Browse functions and help metadata.
Inspect symbolic expression trees, assumptions, traces, and compiled MathIR.
Render SVG plots accurately.
Support plot zoom, pan, fit, and export.
Provide native open/save dialogs and drag-and-drop.
Detect external file modifications.
Support native keyboard accessibility and screen readers.
Support system font scaling and high-DPI displays.
Demonstrate the absence of a localhost HTTP listener and embedded web runtime.
Share the same generated input across both implementations.
rows.note: One generated script per case is submitted to both runners with identical argv and stdin.

rows.title: Generate valid and invalid syntax, numerical boundaries, arrays, symbolic expressions, and errors.
rows.note: The generator covers arithmetic, precision, arrays, symbolic, records, errors, syntax and registry cases (observed category table).

rows.title: Vary precision, budgets, plugin sets, and execution modes.
rows.note: Cases carry args (precision/budgets) and the runner flags are validated against the oracle.

rows.title: Compare exact results, kinds, metadata, diagnostics, and envelopes.
rows.note: The comparator is structural over the whole envelope; the selftest proves it detects a flipped value, a dropped key, a changed scalar and a reordered array.

rows.title: Ignore only explicitly documented volatile fields.
rows.note: Exactly four volatile keys are normalised (revision, elapsed, elapsedTime, timings); a selftest corruption of any other field is reported.

rows.title: Minimize failing inputs automatically.
rows.note: A delta-debugging minimiser reduces a failing script while the same first difference persists; observed minimised examples in the run report.

rows.title: Save reproducible seeds and minimized examples.
rows.note: Runs are seeded and stored with a manifest; regression files record the script and observed difference.

rows.title: Promote every verified mismatch into permanent regression coverage.
rows.note: 33 mismatches were promoted to parity/diff/regressions and are replayed at the start of every run.

rows.title: Run at least 5,000 comparisons per PR and 100,000 nightly.
Fail when either oracle cannot execute.
rows.note: A missing Rust binary and an empty corpus both exit 2; the oracle missing is checked by the same precondition.

rows.title: Preserve all 16 C# DSP builtins and their signatures.
Match convolution, DFT, FFT, filtering, and moving average.
rows.note: DFT matches the oracle on the golden case; convolution/FFT/filter/moving-average differential coverage is not established.

rows.title: Match signal constructors, including impulse, step, cosine, exponential, power series, and noise.
Match delay, scale, and complex component operations.
Preserve argument coercion and argument-position error reporting.
Match precision-dependent optimized paths and arbitrary-precision fallbacks.
Preserve deterministic seeded noise generation.
Preserve cancellation during long operations.
Run the original DSP test suite and differential signal-processing benchmarks.
Resolve the documented ambiguity in noise overloads explicitly, without silently changing the frozen C# behavior.
Every row must resolve to one or more Rust modules, with tests linked to the corresponding C# capabilities.
rows.note: Every project has a disposition and a Rust path or a reason; test-level linkage is 0%.

rows.title: A complete parity run must prove that all required subsystems are present, even if their APIs have been reorganized.
rows.note: Six projects are explicitly absent and eight partial; presence of all required subsystems is therefore disproved, not proven.

rows.title: Inventory all externally visible C# types and methods, not just language builtins.
Identify external consumers: command-line scripts, applications, plugins, automation, and agent harnesses.
Preserve the semantics of public operations, including defaults, error conditions, and value conversions.
Provide equivalent Rust extension points for the C# abstractions that are intended to survive migration.
Explicitly decide whether any .NET consumers require continued compatibility through a C ABI, FFI bridge, or C# wrapper.
rows.note: No decision recorded on .NET consumer compatibility (C ABI, FFI bridge or wrapper).

rows.title: Inventory persisted formats and ensure existing files remain readable or have a verified migration path.
rows.note: No inventory of persisted formats (Studio sessions/settings, knowledge graphs, plots) and no migration path.

rows.title: Preserve every published value kind and its widening rules.
rows.note: Value kinds and widening match across the fixtures; Text comparison still diverges (OBS-013).

rows.title: Match variables, assignments, scopes, closures, recursion, and function calls.
Preserve the _ last-result variable.
Match loops, control flow, and statement evaluation order.
Preserve per-engine precision and plugin state isolation.
rows.note: Engine precision now follows the plugin budget (30) as the reference does; per-engine isolation across concurrent engines is untested.

rows.title: Implement consistent revision and state-publication semantics.
rows.note: A failed or cancelled run publishes a different committed variable set than the oracle (OQ-013).

rows.title: Preserve partial execution, failure, and cancellation behavior.
Match recursion, allocation, rendering, and evaluation budgets.
rows.note: The documented deepest accepted recursion f(85) overflows the Rust runner stack (exit -1073741571); all 39 Recursion cases stay deferred.

rows.title: Publish per-statement execution status and timing information.
rows.note: Per-statement status and timing entries are published with the same shape.

rows.title: Produce deterministic output across repeated runs and different thread counts.
Preserve the complete builtin help and capability catalogue.
rows.note: The capabilities fixture passes: the full builtin help/capability catalogue matches.

rows.title: Test all language behaviors through public engine entry points, not only internal helpers.
Change a decimal period boundary.
Change a numeric widening rule.
Break a Unicode source position.
Remove an envelope field.
Alter a diagnostic code.
Change symbolic canonical ordering.
Break final-digit rounding.
Duplicate captured print() output.
Remove builtin registry metadata.
Disable a precision cap.
Delete a supposedly ported test.
Run the gate with an empty or incomplete corpus.
rows.note: The empty-corpus case exits 2; the mutation harness that proves it is not yet run.

rows.title: Immutable top-level objective: the migration's definition of done cannot be narrowed by an implementation agent.
rows.note: The contract document plus the 262-row ledger make a dropped requirement a gate failure.

rows.title: Coverage-driven planning: select work from unsatisfied parity requirements.
Independent falsification: every significant implementation claim is checked independently.
rows.note: The intent audit is independent, and every agent claim was re-run; not every claim was re-derived.

rows.title: Evidence provenance: claims must include commits, commands, exit codes, and test artifacts.
rows.note: Every journal claim carries a file:line or a command plus its observed output.

rows.title: Distinguish progress from completion.
rows.note: The scorecard reports coverage and gate state separately from progress claims.

rows.title: Persistent failures: unresolved differences remain in the ledger across rounds and context compaction.
rows.note: Unresolved differences and unverified paths live as OQ/RISK rows in the journal and as unmet/partial ledger rows.

rows.title: No fabricated green: missing tools, skipped checks, and unavailable platforms are reported as unverified or failed.
rows.note: Unavailable checks (C# testhost, doctests temp) are recorded as capabilities, not passes.

rows.title: Controlled scope changes: changes to a public contract or exclusion policy require user approval.
Reproducible benchmarking.
Final release auditor: a dedicated final gate evaluates the entire migration from the frozen source of truth.
Work preservation: each completed phase produces a reviewable commit or PR, test evidence, and an updated manifest.
rows.note: Work products are on disk and reviewable; no commit has been made yet.

rows.title: No circular verification: a generated implementation and its generated tests cannot be the only two sources supporting a parity claim.
Port the observation-driven sampling pipeline.
Preserve deterministic seeded generation.
Implement observation canonicalization and behavioral-plane classification.
Implement reduction, convergence, boundaries, and frontiers.
Preserve graph persistence formats.
Implement the config, sample, reduce, converge, query, and help commands.
Match the JSON-over-stdio command protocol and exit codes.
Reproduce the seeded C# graph with seed 20240617.
Verify the Rust knowledge tool against the real Rust runner rather than a mock.
Compare graph outputs and convergence metrics against the frozen C# implementation.
Match the complete token set, including Unicode edge cases.
Match operator precedence and associativity.
rows.note: Unary minus binds tighter than ^ in Rust: -2^2 is 4 where the oracle gives -4. OQ-016.

rows.title: Match literal syntax, string interpolation, ranges, indexing, and slicing.
Match whitespace, newline, comment, and escape handling.
Preserve source positions in UTF-16 code units.
Preserve parse errors, including codes, messages, and locations.
Reject excessive AST/input depth in the same manner as the reference.
Support the complete versioned MathIR node set and text format.
Match lowering, optimization, type inference, and validation.
Preserve common-subexpression handling and emitted ordering where published.
Match lower, compile, compile_full, evalir, and evalir_batch.
Preserve precision and cancellation behavior during evaluation.
Verify direct execution against lowered-then-executed results.
Reject malformed or unsupported IR identically.
Add direct MathIR tests, addressing the original C# test-coverage gap.
All constructors and parsing forms match C# behavior.
Canonical zero representation; no negative zero.
Exact addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and remainder.
rows.note: Addition, subtraction and multiplication are exact; the pow and division conventions are not yet parity-complete (see NUM-004/NUM-005).

rows.title: Signed division uses the same quotient and remainder convention as C#.
Underflow, division by zero, invalid input, and overflow of bounded conversions produce equivalent failures.
rows.note: Violated: Integer.Pow(0) throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException in the oracle but returns 1 in Rust, and 0^3 throws in the oracle but returns 0 (OBS-010, OQ-009).

rows.title: Exact power, factorial, and decimal shifting.
Decimal parse/format round trips for arbitrarily large values.
Identical results regardless of algorithm-selection threshold or worker count.
Test every multiplication/division algorithm against an independent arithmetic oracle.
Benchmark algorithm transitions, not merely steady-state performance.
Benchmark identical inputs and compare matching output digests.
Use warmed executions and account for C# JIT effects.
Report distributions rather than a single sample.
Benchmark both implementations on the same machine and software environment.
Measure arithmetic at small, medium, large, and algorithm-transition sizes.
Include the original numeric, DSP, array, precision, and symbolic benchmark families.
Profile allocations, peak memory, startup time, and latency.
Record all results, inputs, build profiles, and hardware details.
Meet the existing migration target of at least 80% of reference throughput, unless a specific deviation is approved.
Never replace a correctness failure with a performance-based justification.
Implement the functional equivalent of IModusPlugin and IModusContext.
Preserve explicit per-host plugin loading.
Preserve per-engine plugin state; assumptions from one engine must never leak into another.
Preserve builtin registration metadata: name, category, arity, parameters, signature, description, examples, and related functions.
rows.note: Builtin registration metadata (name, category, arity, parameters, signature, summary, examples, related) matches in capabilities and the functions array.

rows.title: Preserve typed-array field and kernel registration.
Keep value conversions owned by the host/kernel boundary.
Compare the complete C# and Rust registries automatically.
rows.note: The registry is compared through the capabilities fixture and the envelope functions array; a dedicated registry diff tool is not built.

rows.title: Verify plugin behavior under multiple concurrently active engines.
Preserve the pinned Lean project and ensure it builds.
Map each relevant theorem to Rust implementation-boundary property tests.
Document the correspondence between the Rust numeric representation and the proof model.
Include exhaustive small-domain arithmetic verification in CI.
Preserve arbitrary decimal precision and exactness metadata.
Preserve repeating-decimal notation, including shortest-period canonicalization.
Match exactness propagation through operations and conversions.
Preserve rounding, truncation, guard-digit, and computation-cap semantics.
Preserve precision changes during execution and their scope.
Implement and verify sqrt, pi, powers, and supported transcendental functions.
Test precision boundaries at 8, 16, 20, 50, 1,000, and 2,500 decimal places.
Preserve the distinction between exact and inexact identity results.
Implement normalized rational fractions with positive denominators and coprime numerator/denominator.
rows.note: No dedicated Rational type (consolidated into Real, permitted by S1.2), but the projection publishes the correct lowest-terms numerator/denominator for every probed periodic value, including preperiods.

rows.title: Add direct Rational tests, since the C# project lacks a dedicated test suite.
Frozen reference: Establish an immutable C# oracle commit or tag. All comparisons must identify its SHA.
rows.note: Immutable oracle pinned at 1cc28f2; verify script refuses dirty C# sources.

rows.title: Complete inventory: Every C# production project, public capability, test, executable, and relevant artifact must have an explicit Rust disposition.
rows.note: Projects and tests are inventoried with dispositions; public C# types/methods are not yet inventoried one by one (ECO-003).

rows.title: Observable equivalence: Compare results at public boundaries; internal algorithms and memory representations may differ.
Strict parity: Mathematical equivalence alone is insufficient when the public contract guarantees a specific textual or structured representation.
No silent exclusions: Unsupported features must appear in a machine-readable coverage manifest.
rows.note: parity/requirements.json records all 262 IDs plus 7 ID-less obligations with owners and phases.

rows.title: Explicit deviations: Intentional behavioral changes require a documented decision, a reason, affected tests, and the user's approval.
Independent verification: Implementation agents cannot be the sole authority validating their own work.
Fail-closed gates: Missing tests, missing reference binaries, skipped oracle runs, and unexecuted checks must not count as passes.
rows.note: Fail-closed guards exist for the oracle and the differential corpus; not every gate is falsified yet.

rows.title: No premature cutover: C# remains the reference implementation until every mandatory gate passes.
Reproducibility: The final state must be reproducible from a clean checkout on CI infrastructure.
-eval — Evaluate supplied source
-file — Evaluate file, preserving source positions
-stdin — Accept piped source and BOM handling
rows.note: Piped source works and matches the oracle; BOM handling is a known oracle/spec conflict (OQ-002), so the row pins the oracle behaviour.

rows.title: Bare script path — Equivalent file execution
-json, --text — Correct output modes
-omit-functions, --omit-variables — Publish empty arrays without changing evaluation
-functions [pattern] — Live registry query without evaluating a script
-function <name> — Full builtin descriptor lookup
-function-limit <n> — Bounded registry results and correct counts
-cancel-after <ms> — Deadline, cancellation state, and budget accounting
rows.note: Deadline, cancellation state (budgetMs/exceeded/stopped) and budget accounting match. The envelope-level committed-state difference (_ published for the completed statement) remains open as OQ-013/ENG-006.

rows.title: -print-budget <n> — Structured truncation with accurate metadata
-plot-dir, --plot-file — Matching plot placement and naming
rows.note: Plot placement and naming match (result path, plot.path, artifacts kind/path). SVG content parity remains open as OQ-012 / WIRE-015 / DESK-022.

rows.title: -help, -h — Supported help surface
rows.note: --help matches the oracle observably (exit 0, usage text).

rows.title: Invalid arguments — Correct diagnostics, stderr, and exit status
rows.note: Invalid arguments exit 2 with a diagnostic containing the offending argument.

rows.title: cargo fmt --check passes.
rows.note: cargo-fmt is not installed for the pinned stable toolchain; the check could not be performed (unverified, not passed).

rows.title: Clippy passes with warnings treated as errors.
rows.note: cargo-clippy is not installed for the pinned stable toolchain; the check could not be performed (unverified, not passed).

rows.title: All tests pass in debug and release profiles.
No floating point is used in the exact numeric value path.
Every unsafe block is isolated, justified, and reviewed.
Dependencies are audited for license and security advisories.
Public APIs have usable documentation and examples.
Build and test workflows work from a clean checkout.
Reproducible release artifacts are produced for every supported target.
CI tests real binaries through their published entry points.
Preserve the plugin's identity and opt-in registration.
Provide equivalent typed-array kernel dispatch.
Preserve exact Real-field addition and active precision.
Test fallback behavior and verify equivalence between the specialized and generic array paths.
Preserve expression kinds, domains, assumptions, and exactness.
Match canonical ordering and hashing-independent canonicalization.
Preserve structural expression identity and interning behavior where observable.
Preserve textual and canonical expression formats.
Match simplification and rewriting with their applicable conditions.
Preserve rewrite budgets, termination, trace ordering, and statuses.
Match substitution, expansion, factoring, collection, and cancellation.
Match differentiation, integration, limits, and series.
Preserve solution sets, conditions, completeness, and domain restrictions.
Match polynomial, nonlinear, system, and matrix-solving behaviors.
Match assumptions, contradiction detection, and assumption isolation.
Preserve all structured rich-result record types and field order.
Verify the complete symbolic builtin registry, including metadata.
Retain the existing SymPy differential oracle as an independent correctness check.
Pin a C# oracle SHA/tag.
rows.note: Pinned SHA in parity/oracle.json and verified by build-oracle.ps1 -Verify.

rows.title: Build and execute the C# reference in CI.
Prevent untracked reference changes.
rows.note: Untracked or modified files in the pinned source directories make verification exit 2.

rows.title: Record approved oracle amendments.
Archive oracle binaries or build inputs for reproducibility.
rows.note: oracle-verified.json records the commit and the DLL SHA-256; the binary itself is not archived.

rows.title: Generate parity/census.json from all original C# tests.
rows.note: parity/census.json is generated by a reflection tool: 15 projects, 2105 methods, 6209 cases, deterministic SHA.

rows.title: Maintain parity/manifest.toml mapping every C# test to a Rust equivalent or approved exclusion.
rows.note: Every case is dispositioned; 3 074 map to a Rust test (49.51 %); 3 135 remain deferred, so the strict mapping obligation is still open (OQ-014).

rows.title: Resolve each mapped Rust test to an actual test that ran.
rows.note: The manifest gate resolves all 262 claimed Rust tests against the measured inventory and requires the suite exit code to be 0.

rows.title: Detect missing, duplicate, renamed, or ignored tests.
rows.note: The census and manifest gates reject duplicate ids and orphan rows; rename/ignore detection is not implemented.

rows.title: Require explicit reasons for every exclusion.
rows.note: An exclusion requires a reason and owner=user; no exclusion exists yet, so the rule is unexercised.

rows.title: Disallow weakening assertions while porting tests.
Report coverage separately by subsystem.
rows.note: parity/coverage.md reports cases, ported, deferred and coverage per C# subsystem from the manifest the gate reads.

rows.title: Require the inventory to remain complete when the oracle changes.
Preserve protocolVersion, symbolicFormatVersion, and mathIrVersion with the same types and values as C#.
rows.note: protocolVersion/symbolicFormatVersion/mathIrVersion match the oracle in 19 of 20 fixtures.

rows.title: Match all success-envelope fields, including result, variables, functions, output, artifacts, revision, and timing data.
rows.note: Every success-envelope field (result, variables, functions, output, artifacts, revision, timing) is compared structurally on 12 green CLI rows.

rows.title: Match all error-envelope fields: code, category, message, recoverable, diagnostics, and applicable resolution information.
rows.note: Error envelopes match on RUN-002 and fixtures/error_envelope (code, category, message, recoverable, diagnostics).

rows.title: Preserve the distinction between an omitted optional JSON field, an explicit Null structured value, and an empty collection.
rows.note: fixtures/absent_field passes: omitted field vs Null vs empty collection are distinguished.

rows.title: Match nested projections for every supported value kind.
rows.note: Every value-kind projection in the 20 fixtures matches, and the exact-rational counterexample (1/6) now matches on the wire.

rows.title: Preserve declared enum types. SolveStatus.Partial and Completeness.Partial must remain distinguishable.
rows.note: The record fixtures cross status/completeness/exactness as declared Enum types, so SolveStatus.Partial and Completeness.Partial are distinguishable.

rows.title: Preserve field order in typed records and ordering of published variables and functions.
rows.note: Record fields are an ordered array and match element by element.

rows.title: Preserve human display, typed, and machine structured representations independently.
rows.note: display, typed and structured are compared independently in every fixture.

rows.title: Capture print() output in the envelope; stdout must contain exactly one JSON document.
rows.note: print_purity passes: print output is captured in the envelope and stdout is one JSON document.

rows.title: Publish the full timing contract, including structural duration and per-statement timing entries.
rows.note: elapsedTime and per-statement timings are present with the same shape (values are the declared volatile keys).

rows.title: Preserve the C# runner's exit-code contract: success 0, script failure 1, usage error 2.
rows.note: Exit codes 0, 1 and 2 are exercised and compared by the CLI gate.

rows.title: Preserve UTF-16 positions, including multibyte Unicode, surrogate pairs, BOM, and CRLF handling.
rows.note: UTF-16 positions/line/column match on fixtures/error_envelope and RUN-002.

rows.title: Match the C# serializer's non-ASCII escaping rules where byte compatibility is required.
rows.note: Parsed JSON matches, and a raw probe showed both runners escaping non-ASCII as \uXXXX; byte-for-byte output is not gated.

rows.title: Match structured truncation rules and differentiate depth, node, and precision caps.
rows.note: --print-budget is implemented and matches the oracle on RUN-011; depth and precision caps are not separately exercised.

rows.title: Preserve artifact behavior for plots, including failure after a previous plotting statement.
rows.note: Artifact kind/path/naming now match; the rendered SVG content does not (OQ-012).
